chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadith, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdillah, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him, 'What is sufficient of the recitation in bowing and prostration?' He said, 'Three glorifications (Tasbihat) with a relaxed pace, and one complete (glorification) are sufficient.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount of dhikr required in ruku and sujud according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the minimum legal sufficiency (kifayah) for the dhikr in ruku' and sujood, offering flexibility between reciting 'Subhana Rabbiyal Azeem' three times with a relaxed pace or a single complete recitation. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of distinguishing between the obligatory minimum (wajib) and the recommended perfection (mustahabb), allowing worshippers to balance brevity with devotion. It highlights the practical leniency granted in daily prayers while maintaining the sanctity of the physical postures.
